study.title: Completion queues: how the NIC tells you work is done
study.what: A ring buffer where the NIC writes a completion entry (CQE) when a work request finishes.
study.how: App posts a WQE and rings the doorbell; the NIC DMA-writes a CQE and flips an ownership bit; the app polls or arms the CQ for an event.
study.why_xlio: XLIO polls CQs from user space instead of waiting on interrupts and the kernel.
study.pitfall: Pure polling burns a core even when idle.
study.question: Why can several QPs share one CQ?
study.answer: Each CQE carries its QP number, so one poll loop can serve many connections.
